h1: SHIN Hotel Victory Monument — a budget hotel on Bangkok's hospital road, within a 7-minute walk of Rajavithi Hospital and the Children's Hospital
intro: If you need to stay several nights close to Rajavithi Hospital or the Queen Sirikit National Institute of Child Health (known locally as the Children's Hospital) and want a clean, modern room at a fair price — SHIN Hotel Victory Monument sits at 507 Ratchawithi Road, the same street the hospitals are on, just about 600 m and a 7–8-minute walk away · a 36-room property in a Japanese minimalist style, clean and well-maintained throughout · free Wi-Fi, free parking, from about THB 900/night · score of 8.9 from 693 verified reviews on Trip.com, putting it above most options at this price in the area.

body.html: Who SHIN Hotel suits best — the hotel stands at 507 Ratchawithi Road, the arterial road that runs through Bangkok's main public-health district, passing Rajavithi Hospital, the Institute of Dermatology, the Queen Sirikit National Institute of Child Health (the Children's Hospital), Phramongkutklao Hospital, and Monk Hospital · SHIN Hotel is about 600 m along this same road, which means that getting to Rajavithi or the Children's Hospital on foot in the morning requires nothing more than walking straight along the pavement — no crossing a main intersection, no waiting for a taxi · the guests who gain the most from this are families staying several days or more while a relative receives treatment, outpatients with repeated appointments across multiple days, and anyone travelling from upcountry who wants a base from which to reach the hospitals on their own two feet · the score of 8.9 from 693 real reviews suggests this hotel is delivering consistently, particularly on cleanliness (9.1) and service (8.9) — the two things that matter most to people staying more than one or two nights.

Location and getting around — Victory Monument is one of Bangkok's most important transit nodes: the BTS interchange at the monument sits at the junction of the Sukhumvit and Silom lines, and the area around it is a hub for intercity minivans serving destinations across Northern, Central and Northeastern Thailand · for travellers arriving from the provinces, being able to step off a minivan and walk to the hotel in about 15 minutes without changing vehicles is a practical advantage that larger, better-known hotel areas further into Bangkok simply cannot match · for the rail network, BTS Victory Monument is about 850 m away, roughly a 10-minute walk, or a 3–5 minute motorbike taxi ride · Ratchaprarop Station on the Airport Rail Link is around 1.4 km, a 15-minute walk or short ride — useful for guests flying in or out of Suvarnabhumi · the streets around the hotel are lined with local restaurants, street-food vendors, and convenience stores, so finding food at any time of day is simple and affordable.

"Stayed five nights while my daughter was being treated at the Children's Hospital. Walking there every morning took less than ten minutes and I never had to wait for transport. The room was spotless. The staff were kind and patient every single day. This is exactly what you need when you're worried about a sick child."

Rooms and design — SHIN Hotel has 36 rooms in a Japanese minimalist style that prioritises cleanliness and calm over decorative complexity · the standard Double has a king bed, air-conditioning, a fridge, a smart TV, free Wi-Fi and an en-suite bathroom · the Superior Twin has two separate single beds (28 sqm) — well suited for two family members taking turns at the hospital, or a parent and older child sharing without wanting to share a bed · the Quadruple Room with bunk beds (25–27 sqm) gives groups or larger families the option of fitting more people into one room at a lower per-person cost · the detail that comes up most often in real reviews is the cleanliness and freshness of the rooms relative to the price — multiple guests note it is the cleanest hotel they have experienced in Thailand in this price bracket, which is a meaningful claim in a city with considerable competition.

Facilities worth knowing about — SHIN Hotel has no pool and no restaurant, which is standard for a 36-room property in this price range; it compensates with things that genuinely matter in a hospital-stay context · free Wi-Fi throughout, reliable enough to video-call family back home, send documents, and keep up with medical-appointment schedules · free parking, which is notable — most hotels in this area charge separately for parking or have no spaces at all · this is a real advantage for families who drove to Bangkok from the provinces or are renting a car to move between hospitals · the front desk operates 24 hours, so late arrivals after an emergency-room visit are straightforward · a THB 300 cash security deposit is collected at check-in and fully refunded at check-out · convenience stores and street-food stalls are within 2–3 minutes' walk in either direction along Ratchawithi Road.

What real guests say — drawing from 693 reviews on Trip.com, ratings on Agoda (score 8.9 from over 1,000 reviews), and guest feedback on Hostelworld, the picture is consistent: on the positive side, staff are praised strongly for patience and helpfulness — particularly around giving directions to the hospitals and helping late-arriving guests settle in · room cleanliness is a near-universal compliment; several reviewers call it the cleanest budget stay they've had in Bangkok · the quiet atmosphere in the evenings is noted as a genuine plus for people exhausted after long hospital days · on the critical side: Ratchawithi Road is a main artery, and rooms facing the street can pick up traffic noise at night — guests sensitive to sound should request an inward-facing room · a handful of reviews mention morning sun exposure in rooms with east-facing windows, which is resolved by keeping the curtains drawn · one report of bed bugs in a dormitory room surfaced on Trip.com; the hotel investigated and found no infestation, and there are no corroborating reports across other platforms.

"Clean beyond what I expected for the price. The Japanese minimalist decor makes it feel calm and organised, which is exactly what you need after a stressful day at the hospital. Walking to Rajavithi in the morning was easy and stress-free. Parking was free too — that matters when you have driven from the provinces."

Price and value — SHIN Hotel's starting price in a normal period runs from about THB 900–1,100/night for a standard room, rising to around THB 1,300–1,500 during high season and long public holidays · at this price, the cleanliness standard and Japanese minimalist atmosphere clearly exceed what most similarly priced hotels in the Victory Monument area offer · the free parking makes the deal stronger for anyone with a car · for longer stays of five to seven nights, promotional rates are often available through booking platforms — comparing Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com before committing will usually reveal a better rate than the walk-in price · Trip.com in particular sometimes shows this hotel at around USD 27–39 per night depending on the season.

honestSummary: SHIN Hotel Victory Monument is the strongest budget option on Ratchawithi Road for anyone who needs to walk to Rajavithi Hospital or the Children's Hospital without relying on transport every morning — clean rooms, helpful staff, free parking and an honest score of 8.9 from nearly 700 real reviews · the main limitation is traffic noise from street-facing rooms at night, and the absence of a pool or dining room · for its target audience — families accompanying patients, outpatients with repeated appointments, and provincial visitors using Victory Monument as a transit hub — those trade-offs are easy to accept.
honestChecks: If you are sensitive to traffic noise — Ratchawithi Road carries traffic at night, and street-facing rooms feel it · request an inward-facing room or a higher floor when booking, and have earplugs as backup.

If you want a pool or a restaurant — SHIN Hotel is a rest-and-sleep property with none of these · if your budget allows THB 1,200+ and you'd value a rooftop pool, De Prime Rangnam Hotel a short ride away is worth comparing.

If you are arriving as a group with heavy luggage — the standard rooms are compact · book a Twin or Quadruple room to avoid feeling crowded, and confirm with the front desk that luggage storage is available on arrival day.

tips.title: Walk west along Ratchawithi Road
tips.body: Leave the hotel and walk west along Ratchawithi Road — you will reach the Queen Sirikit Children's Hospital first, then Rajavithi Hospital, in about 600 m without crossing a major junction. No ride needed on a clear morning.

tips.title: Request an inward-facing room if noise matters
tips.body: Rooms on the street side can pick up traffic sound at night. Ask for an inward-facing room or a higher floor when booking — the front desk will try to accommodate if you mention it in advance.

tips.title: Victory Monument — the intercity van hub
tips.body: The roundabout at Victory Monument is Bangkok's main departure point for minivans to Northern, Central and Northeastern Thailand. From this hotel, the hub is about a 10–15-minute walk or a short motorbike-taxi ride, making it easy to get home without going to a main terminal.

tips.title: Bring THB 300 cash for the security deposit
tips.body: The hotel collects a THB 300 cash security deposit at check-in, refunded in full at check-out. It is not an extra charge — just make sure you have small notes available when you arrive.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — SHIN Hotel Victory Monument

faq.q: How far is SHIN Hotel Victory Monument from Rajavithi Hospital?
faq.a: SHIN Hotel is at 507 Ratchawithi Road, the same road as the hospital. Rajavithi Hospital is about 600 m away — roughly a 7–8-minute walk along the pavement, with no major road crossings needed. The Queen Sirikit National Institute of Child Health (Children's Hospital) is at a similar distance, slightly closer.

faq.q: What is the price range at SHIN Hotel Victory Monument?
faq.a: Prices start from about THB 900/night for a Standard Double in the low season · the Superior Twin and Quadruple rooms are slightly higher · during high season and public holidays prices rise to around THB 1,300–1,500 · comparing Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com before booking usually reveals the best available rate.

faq.q: Does SHIN Hotel have free parking?
faq.a: Yes — on-site parking is free for all guests, which is notably rare for hotels in this price range in the Ratchawithi Road area. This makes SHIN Hotel a particularly practical choice for families who have driven to Bangkok from the provinces or are renting a car.

faq.q: Is SHIN Hotel Victory Monument suitable for families accompanying patients?
faq.a: Very much so. The walking distance to Rajavithi and the Children's Hospital, the free parking, the clean quiet rooms, and the affordable price all make this property a strong practical match for families who need to stay multiple nights while a relative is receiving treatment. The Twin and Quadruple room types accommodate two or more guests without needing to book separate rooms.

faq.q: How far is SHIN Hotel from BTS Victory Monument station?
faq.a: BTS Victory Monument station is about 850 m away, approximately a 10-minute walk. A motorbike taxi from the hotel to the station takes 3–5 minutes and costs around THB 15–20. From Victory Monument BTS, you can transfer to the full BTS network covering central Bangkok.

faq.q: Which hospitals are within easy reach of SHIN Hotel Victory Monument?
faq.a: Ratchawithi Road is Bangkok's principal public-health corridor. From SHIN Hotel, Rajavithi Hospital and the Queen Sirikit Children's Hospital are walkable (7–8 min). Phramongkutklao Hospital is about 5 minutes by taxi or motorbike. Ramathibodi Hospital (Mahidol University) is about 7 minutes by car. This cluster of hospitals is the main reason families with medical appointments choose to stay in this area.
